title: Series, Parallel, Air Gaps & The B-H Curve
subtitle: This is where you actually solve magnetic circuit problems. The B-H curve links H to B for each material and is used in every multi-material problem. The air gap always dominates — a 2mm gap typically needs more MMF than 100mm of steel.

topics.title: Series Circuits, Air Gaps & Ampere's Circuital Law

subtopics.title: Series Circuits, Air Gaps & Ampere's Circuital Law

content.text: In a series magnetic circuit, the same flux φ passes through all sections. Ampere's Circuital Law: NI = Σ(HᵢLᵢ) — sum H×L for every section around the loop. That total = MMF provided by the coil.
For an air gap: no B-H curve. Use H_gap = B/μ₀ = 7.96×10⁵ × B directly. Because air has μᵣ=1, even a tiny gap dominates the circuit.

1. Find B = φ/A (same for all sections in series) 2. From B-H curve: read H for each iron/steel section 3. For air gap: H_gap = B/μ₀ = 7.96×10⁵ × B 4. Ampere's Law: NI = H_core×L_core + H_gap×L_gap + ... 5. Solve for I = NI/N
Common mistake — Trying to use a B-H curve for air — there isn't one. For air ALWAYS use H_gap = B/μ₀ = 7.96×10⁵ × B. Memorise this.

content.text: The B-H curve links field intensity H (applied) to flux density B (result) for a material. Starts linear, curves over at saturation. Materials: Sheet steel (highest μ), Cast steel (medium), Cast iron (lowest, cheapest).

The hysteresis loop shows energy lost as heat when magnetising/demagnetising cyclically. Key points: Bₘ (saturation), Bᵣ (remanence — flux when H=0), Hc (coercive force — H needed to make B=0). Loop area = energy loss per cycle per unit volume.

The distinction that loses exam marks every year:
Eddy current loss: caused by induced circulating currents in solid iron rotating in magnetic field. Remedy: laminate the core (thin insulated layers break up current paths). Hysteresis loss: caused by magnetic domain realignment each cycle. Remedy: use silicon steel (narrow hysteresis loop — material choice, not structural). Laminations → eddy current loss. Silicon steel → hysteresis loss. Never mix these up.
